answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through randomized co-production. The network pairs two identities at random to jointly solve each task, interleaving their contributions in a verifiable chain. A fake cannot choose its partner, so a farm's copies cannot hide among themselves; paired strangers quickly expose copies. Like jade set in timber, trust is built by joining unlike pieces, and an onyx-black fake stands out against a genuine partner. Each extra fake needs its own live, willing partner whose reputation is at stake, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
